messages.subject: define a constant probability
parts:
Hello, 

Let's say that my likelihood is: p1 * p2

where p1 ~ N(x, xerr)

and 

    p2 = 0.823 if t = 0 
                 1   if t = 1

Although statistically it is simple, I am finding troubles to define p2 in PySTAN. My model is:

model = """
data {
        int<lower=0> N; // number of points
        vector[N] x; 
        vector[N] xerr; 
        vector[N] t; // indicator: elements are 0 or 1
    }

parameters {
        real alpha;
        real beta;
    }

model {
        vector[N] p2;
    
        // PRIORS
        alpha ~ normal(0,10);
        beta ~ normal(0,10);
    
        p1 ~ normal(x, xerr);
    
       // first attempt
       for (i in 1:N) {
           if (t[i] == 1)
                p2[i] ~ 0.823;
           else if (t[i] == 0)
                p2[i] ~ 1;
        }
}
"""
However, this model failed. So in my second attempt I defined p2 as follows:

// second attempt

for (i in 1:N) {

    if (cnd[i] == 1)

         p2[i] ~ uniform(0, 1.0 / 0.823); // 1.0 / (1.0/0.823 - 0) = 0.823

    else if (cnd[i] == 0)

        p2[i] ~ uniform(0,1); // 1.0 / (1.0 - 0) = 1

}


This model failed too. Any suggestions on how I can write my model in PySTAN? 


Thanks!

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] define a constant probability
parts:
I'm not sure why you want to do that, but I think I understand
what you want. You want to use increment_log_prob(). Stan works
on the log scale, so if your likelihood is p1 * p2, your log
likelihood is log p1 + log p2.

So you just want:

y ~ normal(mu, sigma);

Note that the y on the left of the twiddle is the outcome, not the
log probability --- that gets added implicitly. Or you can write this
to make it clearer:

increment_log_prob(normal_log(y, mu, sigma));

which has the same effect.

Then for the conditional, you have:

if (t == 0)
increment_log_prob(log(0.823));

You don't need to add log(1), as it's zero.

But either way, it won't do anything to the posterior as
it's just a bunch of constants not involving parameters.

- Bob

If the indicator I = 0, then I have a 17.7% (1-0.177 = 0.823) chance that the object is a false positive. Is there a way to force STAN to take this probability (even though it is constant) into consideration?

Thanks a lot for your help Bob, appreciated! :)

If the indicator I = 0, then I have a 17.7% (1-0.177 = 0.823) chance that the object is a false positive. Is there a way to force STAN to take this probability (even though it is constant) into consideration?

Stan will add it to the log density, but given that it's
constant, it doesn't affect the posterior, so it'll have
no effect. That's the right thing for Stan to do here --- follow
the math of the posterior.

Stan drops constant terms from sampling statements such as

y ~ normal(0, 10);

where it won't bother adding -log(10) to the log density for the sd
term.

- Bob
